content.text: No MFN construct exists anywhere in this agreement — the only "not less favorable" language concerns lender subordination terms in SFJ's favour, not any obligation on PB to extend best terms.

input.quote: enter into a new subordination agreement with a new lender(s) on terms and conditions that are taken as a whole not less favorable in any material respect to SFJ than those set forth in the subordination agreement to be entered into with SVB
input.rationale: We searched the agreement for every MFN-type mechanic (most-favoured-nation, "more/no less favorable", right of first refusal/negotiation, matching or best-terms obligations, comparable/equivalent terms) and found none that burdens PB. The only "not less favorable" language, at Section 7.5 (p0543), is a financing covenant requiring any replacement lender's subordination agreement to be no less favorable to SFJ than the SVB subordination agreement — a subordination benchmark tied to a single refinancing document, not an obligation for PB to extend SFJ terms given to third parties or to match a third-party offer. The Licensing Transaction covenant (7.5.5) is a consent/Material Impact mechanic, not an MFN, and any consent restriction there belongs to a different rule. The agreement therefore meets the preferred position: PB has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting SFJ. No redline proposed.
